'''''Symphoricarpos orbiculatus''''', commonly called '''coralberry''',<ref name=USDA>{{PLANTS|id=SYOR|taxon=Symphoricarpos orbiculatus|accessdate=6 December 2015}}</ref> '''buckbrush''' or '''Indian currant''' is a woody species of flowering plant in the [[Caprifoliaceae|honeysuckle family]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/8370347#page/214 |last=Jones |first=George Neville |date=1940 |title=A monograph of the genus ''Symphoricarpos'' |journal=Journal of the Arnold Arboretum |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=201–252}}</ref>

==Description==
''Symphoricarpos orbiculatus'' is an erect, rhizomatous shrub. The leaves are typically oval shaped and arranged oppositely along the branches.<ref name=Virginia/> The leaves are sessile or subsessile. The flowers are greenish-white and borne in verticils in the leaf axils. The fruit is a purple-red [[drupe]] with two stones; the drupes are persistent through winter. ''Symphoricarpos orbiculatus'' can reach a height of {{cvt|6|ft|cm|-1}}, but is typically {{cvt|3|–|4|ft|cm|-1}}.<ref name=Virginia>{{cite web |url=http://www.ppws.vt.edu/scott/weed_id/supor.htm |title=Coral-Berry, Indian Currant, Devil's Shoestring, or Buckbrush |website=Virginia Tech Weed Identification Guide |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917122837/http://www.ppws.vt.edu/scott/weed_id/supor.htm |archive-date=2013-09-17}}</ref> The plant is monoecious, with male and female flowers on the same individual.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://garden.org/plants/view/79123/Coralberry-Symphoricarpos-orbiculatus/|title=Plant database entry for Coralberry (Symphoricarpos orbiculatus) with 24 images, 2 comments, and 50 data details}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Symphoricarpos orbiculatus'' is native to the eastern and central United States as well as central Canada ([[Ontario]]) and northeastern Mexico ([[Coahuila]], [[Nuevo León]]).<ref name=USDA/><ref>{{BONAP |genus=Symphoricarpos |species=orbiculatus |date=2014}}</ref><ref>{{GRIN}}</ref>
